notes: Odd-electron metal fragments (open-shell plan P4 step 1). A row is element and oxidation state (domain.oxidation_state: formal charge + H on M + bond orders to non-metals) with an optional donor condition, matched in order; it holds for a species only where spin_table's rule C has A and B agree on the row's count. donors_any: the row applies only when a donor (a neighbour, or H on the metal) is one of these; donors_none: it does not apply when one is.

rows.basis: Cu(II) oxidizes iodide and hydride: Cu2+ with I- gives CuI and I2 (CuI2 is not a stable compound), and a Cu(II) hydride reduces itself; the drawing has no species to compute
Cu(II) is d9: one d hole, S = 1/2 in any geometry, by count

Fe(III) is d5; without a donor from the strong-field end of the spectrochemical series (C and P donors: CN-, CO, phosphines) it is high spin, S = 5/2 (FeX4-, FeX3, FeCl3.L); with one, low spin is possible and there is no row
